ab_test_design.claim_boundary: Experiment design only; no predicted winner, CTR, or success probability.
constants: same test window controlled by native tool
ab_test_design.evaluation: Use native YouTube A/B test output; winner selection is based primarily on watch-time share, not external CTR-only judgment.
ab_test_design.meaningful_difference: Each set contrasts curiosity/feasibility, scale/mechanism, and consequence/contradiction framing rather than wording-only variants.
ab_test_design.scope: Use only if opportunity is produced as eligible long-form. Shorts remain ineligible under current YouTube documentation.
ab_test_design.variable_tested: Combined title and thumbnail package: A, B, and C for one opportunity.

counter_evidence: Limit/measurement title evidence is mostly Shorts: 8 of 9 items; long-form transfer is unproven.
What-if titles are common but mixed: 44 items, 1.0507x median channel-relative performance, with low performers.
Direct question/statement titles are repeatedly weak in this snapshot: 8 items, 0.3833x median.
Consequence questions differ by format: 2.0819x median for 2 long-form items versus 0.6219x for 8 Shorts.
Extreme-condition wording alone is not strong: 25 items, 0.8126x median.
Parenthetical usage occurs once; it is a ONE_OFF_HYPOTHESIS and cannot support a winner archetype.
No historical title-thumbnail relationship is observable because no thumbnail image is locally inspectable.

evidence_snapshot.non_packaging_visual_exclusion: Registered forensic frames depict video content, not thumbnail surfaces.

limitations: One registered public-metric snapshot per item; no performance trajectory.
No impressions, CTR, watch time, retention, traffic source, subscriber conversion, unique viewers, or audience overlap.
Title associations are observational and confounded by topic, thumbnail, format, release context, and content.
Registered thumbnail URLs are references, not locally preserved images; no visual attributes are inferred from them.
Long-form and Shorts evidence remains separated; transfer between formats is unproven.
